claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity relative to a random solid solution in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
SRO can be stabilized by annealing below the order-disorder transition temperature.
Rapid quenching from a high-temperature ordered state can preserve SRO.
The non-random atomic distributions associated with SRO extend over approximately 1–2 nm.
SRO can be introduced while retaining a single-phase BCC structure.
The 300–1000 K test range is below the alloy's order-disorder transition temperature.
SRO clusters are associated with diffuse antiphase boundaries and local lattice-distortion fields.
Diffuse antiphase boundaries and SRO-associated distortion fields act as phonon-scattering centers.
SRO creates a rugged potential-energy landscape.
SRO introduces correlated local variations in atomic mass and bond stiffness relative to the average random environment.
The energetic cost of breaking local chemical order creates a scattering potential for phonons.
Scattering from SRO clusters and their strain fields increases the phonon-scattering rate and reduces phonon mean free path.
In MoNbTaW, SRO hinders screw-dislocation motion but can accelerate edge-dislocation motion.
Any SRO-induced departure from a random potential universally suppresses phonon transport because it produces stronger translational-symmetry breaking than an RSS.
SRO is expected to reduce lattice thermal conductivity by approximately 10–20% relative to the RSS state.
The SRO-induced suppression should be greatest at 300–600 K.
Above approximately 1000 K, the SRO effect may diminish because SRO disorders or Umklapp scattering dominates.
The proposed mechanism applies only while SRO remains stable and does not develop into long-range precipitation.
Electronic thermal conductivity may respond differently from lattice thermal conductivity when SRO changes the electronic structure.
A confirmed nonzero SRO parameter together with lattice thermal conductivity equal to or greater than that of the RSS control would falsify the proposed suppression hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Rapid quenching is presented as a way to preserve an ordered/SRO state in the initial-state description but as a way to retain the RSS state in Batch A. Different pre-quench equilibration temperatures could reconcile these statements, but those distinct starting conditions are not specified.
